title: A count at two scales
stem: A laboratory estimates that each millilitre of a culture contains $3.2\times10^5$ cells, to two significant figures. It transfers exactly $2.5\times10^{-3}$ litres. Treat the transfer volume as exact.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Express the estimated total cell count in standard form.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the interval of possible counts per transfer from the rounding of the quoted concentration. State your convention at a halfway value.

steps.text: With positive halves rounded up the concentration lies in $[3.15,3.25)\times10^5$.
The interval is $[7.875,8.125)\times10^5$ cells. Equivalent answers with a consistent rounding convention receive credit.

subject: math-aa-hl

verification.method: Independent recalculation and mark allocation review
verification.notes: Original 2027–28 cohort practice. Each marking point corresponds to the named part.

title: Reading a logarithmic scale
stem: A sensor records $L=\log_{10}(I/I_0)$ for positive intensities. Its display records $L=2.4$ to one decimal place.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Give the possible interval for $L$, using the usual round-half-up rule, and hence give exact bounds for $I/I_0$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The technician treats the midpoint reading as exact and doubles the intensity. Find the new display reading and determine whether every original intensity would lead to the same new display.

steps.text: Exponentiation with base 10 preserves the inequalities.
Starting from exactly 2.4 gives 2.7 on the display.
Possible new values run from about 2.65103 to 2.75103, so some round to 2.8.
